# User working preferences and scope

Derived from available AutoNation project conversations through September 20, 2026 and the supplied role description, current resume and AutoNation One strategy v5. Retrieval did not establish a complete transcript archive. Use these as defaults; current instructions override them. Preserve user choices separately from assistant proposals.

## Transferable preferences

- Be a copilot during ambiguity and autonomous during execution. Ask about consequential unknowns; avoid forced waiting and repeated confirmation after direction is clear.
- Lead with the business problem and a coherent point of view. Explain why a choice makes sense rather than listing features or frameworks.
- Separate outside-in hypotheses from internal facts and researchable questions. Avoid sounding as though public research proves private operational realities.
- Consider speed, customer decision burden, explicit next-action ownership and handoffs where relevant. Examine actual mandate, resources and decision rights when evaluating an organizational role.
- Favor concise executive writing and purposeful visuals. Preserve substantive distinctions while removing redundant wording. Adapt output to its use: a recruiter question sheet, executive discussion and strategic brief need different depth.
- Connect customer experience to economics and delivery capability. Distinguish strategy, milestones and execution phases. Use benchmarks to inform differentiated choices rather than defaulting to imitation.
- Use a genuinely independent reviewer, explicit rubric and supported rating; iterate on demonstrated defects.

## AutoNation-specific accepted direction; do not impose on other businesses

- AutoNation One is the organizing vision; Carvana is competitive context rather than the headline.
- Later September 20 corrections: preserve the strategic narrative and customer voice; use “Push certainty upstream.” The app is the consumer home and proposed initial beachhead, not the AutoNation One strategy. Retain the new-sales path alongside ownership. For the journey slide, use less text, a connected visual path and requested custom iconography. These are project-specific directions, not universal template requirements.
- Preserve the four customer moments in the current strategy and the lifecycle beyond purchase. The presentation's simplified Shop / Purchase / Delivery / Ownership framing is audience-specific, not a substitute for the full argument everywhere.
- Transformation milestones: Create & Capture Demand; Convert Demand Better; Deepen the Ownership Relationship. Milestone 1 includes existing-customer activation and new-customer top-funnel acquisition. Milestone 3 generates relationship/signals that feed activation in milestone 1.
- Use high-level execution phasing without invented dates in this project. Do not revive the removed “Open the Network” idea. Address negotiation friction as a question to investigate, without prematurely prescribing implementation.
- Ownership extends beyond customer support. Branding requests apply to AutoNation presentation materials. Do not treat an assistant's suggested replacement copy as approved without evidence.
- Re-read the latest role description/resume/strategy when using their contents; do not freeze job titles, performance numbers, financial mix or company capabilities into this skill. Resume metrics differ from some historical summaries.
